//: This database no longer holds anything that decides access. The two access
codes, the proof-of-code records, the trusted-browser registry and the admin
grants all moved to Cloud Firestore, NEXT TO THE MONEY, because Firestore rules
can read a document (accessGrants/{uid}) while Realtime Database rules cannot —
a database that cannot see the trust record cannot enforce it.
The old paths below are kept DENIED on purpose rather than deleted, so a stale
deploy that still points at this file fails closed instead of quietly
re-opening the shop to every anonymous Firebase user. Their data can be deleted
once the new rules are deployed; see the README (Migration).
KNOWN GAP — expenses. expenses/{dateKey}/{expId} is still here, and
'auth != null' is the strongest condition this rule language can express, so ANY
anonymous Firebase user can READ the shop's expenses. They cannot write them
(.write is false), and no rule anywhere trusts this data for money arithmetic.
Moving expenses into Firestore so they sit behind the same trusted() gate is
tracked as the next step; it is called out in the README's known-risks section
rather than left to be discovered.

general.//: Moved to Firestore shop/general. Denied here so a stale deploy cannot rewrite it.

security.//: Held the PLAINTEXT shop code. No longer written; the hash lives in Firestore securitySecrets/shop.

admin.//: Held the PLAINTEXT admin code. No longer written; the hash lives in Firestore securitySecrets/admin.

enrollments.//: Moved to Firestore enrollments/{uid}, where the code is compared against securitySecrets.

devices.//: Moved to Firestore accessGrants/{uid}. The old tokenHash-keyed registry is dead.

admins.//: Moved to Firestore accessGrants/{uid}.role. There is no separate admin collection any more.

expenses.//: Read-only, and readable by any signed-in user — see KNOWN GAP at the top of this file.
